title: typeshyrt
subtitle: Web Design — E-commerce
description: A streetwear label where the storefront behaves like a social feed — scroll the drops, double-tap to open. Bold, monochrome and meme-fluent, designed and built end-to-end on Shopify.

sections.label: Overview
paragraphs: typeshyrt turns internet vernacular into wearable type. Every tee is a single one-liner — group-chat energy, FYP captions, iMessage bubbles — printed clean on heavyweight cotton and sold for a flat $45.

Rather than a conventional shop grid, the storefront is built to feel like scrolling a feed. A stark black canvas, one giant wordmark, and a single prompt: scroll through drops. double-tap to open. The whole experience leans into the brand's native habitat — your phone.
I handled the look end-to-end on Shopify: the monochrome identity, the feed-style browsing, the product pages and the checkout flow.

sections.label: The Storefront
paragraphs: Drops are filed by mood, not category — For You Page, Repost, Quotes, iMessage and Now Playing — so browsing feels like flicking between tabs of an app, not aisles of a shop.

sections.label: The Drops
paragraphs: Each drop is one line of type on a 180gsm relaxed-fit tee. The catalogue reads like a group chat — deadpan, chronically online and very screenshot-able.

sections.label: Palette
paragraphs: One rule: black and white, nothing else. The restraint keeps the focus on the type and lets the photography carry every drop.
